# math.gl

> Modular JavaScript mathematics for 3D and geospatial applications.


## docs

math.gl is an Open Visualization, OpenJS Foundation and Linux Foundation project.

- [Overview](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs.md): math.gl is an Open Visualization, OpenJS Foundation and Linux Foundation project.

### developer-guide

Start with a small calculation, then choose the modules your application needs. math.gl runs on the CPU; its arrays and coordinate utilities can feed a map, a renderer, or an analysis pipeline.

- [Developer Guide](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/developer-guide.md): Start with a small calculation, then choose the modules your application needs. math.gl runs on the CPU; its arrays and coordinate utilities can feed a map, a renderer, or an analysis pipeline.

### modules

- [Packages](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules.md)

#### core

The core package provides vectors, matrices, and rotations for 3D math, plus utilities for colors, UTF-8 text, and Apache Arrow data.

- [@math.gl/core](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core.md): The core package provides vectors, matrices, and rotations for 3D math, plus utilities for colors, UTF-8 text, and Apache Arrow data.
- [Euler](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/euler.md): A class to handle Euler rotation. More information on rotation using a Euler vector can be found here. Generally speaking the three components of the Euler object represents the roll, pitch and yaw angles and the rotation is applied according to a specific rotation order.
- [Local frames](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/local-frame.md): Use @math.gl/core to rotate offsets or velocities between a local
- [MathArray](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/math-array.md): MathArray is the shared array base for core vectors, matrices, quaternions, and Euler angles. Use a concrete class rather than constructing it directly. Mutating methods return the receiver.
- [Matrix](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/matrix.md): Matrix is the shared base for Matrix3 and Matrix4. It extends MathArray and stores elements in column-major order.
- [Matrix3](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/matrix3.md): A 3x3 matrix. Any arguments can be plain JavaScript arrays or other math.gl objects.
- [Matrix4](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/matrix4.md): A 4x4 matrix. Any arguments to Matrix4 methods can be plain JavaScript arrays or other math.gl objects.
- [Numeric helpers](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/numeric-helpers.md): Import these functions from @math.gl/core. Vector functions accept finite 2D, 3D
- [Pose](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/pose.md): A 6-degree-freedom pose (3D position and 3D rotation).
- [Quaternion](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/quaternion.md): Quaternion extends JavaScript Array through its core base classes.
- [SampleTrack](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/sample-track.md): Evaluate timestamped scalar, vector, or quaternion samples with reusable outputs.
- [SphericalCoordinates](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/spherical-coordinates.md): Stores radius, phi, and theta, with angle and geographic convenience accessors. Angles in the primary fields are radians. This class retains legacy conversion conventions; see the conversion limitation below before using it for coordinate exchange.
- [Spheroid conversions](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/spheroid.md): The optional @math.gl/core entry provides low-level conversions between
- [Math Utility Functions](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/utilities.md): Configuration, numeric comparisons, angle conversions, and array helpers for core math.
- [Vector](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/vector.md): Vector is the base class for Vector2, Vector3, and Vector4. It extends MathArray and JavaScript Array; use a concrete vector class.
- [Vector2](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/vector2.md): A two dimensional vector
- [Vector3](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/vector3.md): Vector3 extends JavaScript Array through its core base classes.
- [Vector4](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/api-reference/vector4.md): Stores four numeric components [x, y, z, w]. For homogeneous coordinates, W = 1 represents a point and W = 0 represents a direction under an affine transform.
- [@math.gl/core/arrow](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow.md): Apache Arrow
- [Arrow schema utilities](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/arrow-schema-utils.md): The Arrow schema utilities help validate Apache Arrow JS tables at runtime and rename columns while
- [Arrow table transport](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/arrow-table-transport.md): Use column-buffer transport for worker hops between matching Apache Arrow JS
- [GeoArrow](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/developer-guide/geoarrow.md): GeoArrow stores geometry in typed-array buffers rather than one JavaScript object per row. math.gl describes those buffers with plain TypeScript objects, so the same geometry kernels can work with Apache Arrow, a loader, or application-owned storage without depending on a table runtime.
- [GeoArrow in math.gl](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/geoarrow.md): Use @math.gl/core/arrow to work with geometry columns from Apache Arrow feature tables.
- [@math.gl/core/arrow](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/geoarrow-utils.md): @math.gl/core/arrow includes columnar geospatial math over runtime-neutral descriptors. Importing this combined entry point requires the application-provided Apache Arrow peer; the descriptor kernels operate directly on buffers.
- [GeoArrow API reference](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/geoarrow-utils/api-reference/geoarrow.md): All root functions are synchronous. Unless a function explicitly returns a new column or fills a
- [Indexed Arrow views](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/indexed-arrow-table.md): IndexedArrowTable provides a cheap sorted view of an arrow.Table without
- [MappedArrowTable](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/mapped-arrow-table.md): MappedArrowTable provides a cheap key-value map view of an arrow.Table without
- [splitArrowBuffers](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/split-arrow-buffers.md): splitArrowBuffers rebuilds Apache Arrow JS objects so sliced internal typed-array buffers are
- [@math.gl/core/arrow](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/wkb.md): @math.gl/core/arrow provides synchronous codecs for individual WKB, EWKB, and WKT geometry values. The codec implementation operates independently of GeoArrow descriptors, while importing the combined Arrow entry point requires the application-provided Apache Arrow peer.
- [WKB and WKT API reference](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/arrow/wkb/api-reference/wkb.md): All APIs are synchronous. Inputs are borrowed and never detached or mutated.
- [@math.gl/core/color](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/color.md): @math.gl/core/color provides reusable color conversions, palettes, scale compilation, quantile sketches, and RGB lookup-table sampling. It operates on ordinary values and typed arrays and does not require Apache Arrow or a SQL runtime.
- [Benchmarks](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/developer-guide/benchmarks.md): Run the general math.gl benchmark suite in your browser. Start with Core math for vectors,
- [3D Coordinate Systems](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/developer-guide/coordinate-systems.md): Choose coordinates that fit the operation you need. Core provides Cartesian vectors, spherical coordinates, and homogeneous coordinates for matrix transforms.
- [Floating Point](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/developer-guide/floating-point.md): Rounding can make mathematically equivalent calculations produce slightly different numeric results. Use approximate comparisons for computed coordinates, and exact comparisons when identical stored values are required.
- [Functional math](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/developer-guide/functional-math.md): The class and functional APIs share array-compatible storage, but expose different
- [Homogeneous Coordinates](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/developer-guide/homogeneous-coordinates.md): A four-component vector lets a 4×4 matrix represent translation and perspective along with rotation and scale. Use Vector4 when the homogeneous component w must remain explicit.
- [3D Rotations](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/developer-guide/rotations.md): Use Euler angles to specify an orientation, Quaternion to compose or interpolate rotations, and Matrix4 to combine rotation with translation and scale. All rotation angles in math.gl are in radians.
- [Transformations](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/developer-guide/transformations.md): Use Matrix4 to combine translation, rotation, and scale. Use a quaternion when only rotation is needed. Core vector methods mutate their receiver; matrix transform methods write to a supplied result or allocate a new array.
- [View and Projection Matrices](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/developer-guide/view-and-projection.md): A view matrix expresses world coordinates relative to a camera. A projection matrix maps those camera coordinates to homogeneous clip coordinates. Compose them as projection * view to transform a world-space point.
- [Core Guide](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/guide.md): Guides and background for Core.
- [Preliminaries](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/guide/preliminaries.md): Mathematical foundations for working with transformations and 3D coordinates.
- [@math.gl/core/matrix](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/matrix.md): This entry point exposes the foundational core math API, including vectors, matrices, quaternions, Euler rotations, poses, coordinate conversions, numeric types, and utilities.
- [@math.gl/core/types](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/types.md): @math.gl/core provides shared numeric array, bounds, and spheroid types, plus runtime array checks and Float16 support detection.
- [Array Types](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/types/api-reference/array-types.md): math.gl provides a number of numeric array types.
- [Bounds](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/types/api-reference/bounds.md): Bounds is a type-only union of Bounds2D and Bounds3D. Each uses [minimum, maximum] coordinates.
- [Bounds2D](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/types/api-reference/bounds2d.md): Bounds2D describes an axis-aligned 2D extent as [[minX, minY], [maxX, maxY]].
- [Bounds3D](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/types/api-reference/bounds3d.md): Bounds3D describes an axis-aligned 3D extent as [[minX, minY, minZ], [maxX, maxY, maxZ]].
- [@math.gl/core/utf8](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/core/utf8.md): @math.gl/core/utf8 helps applications work efficiently with binary UTF-8 strings

#### dggs

@math.gl/dggs provides a deliberately small JavaScript API for decoding cell geometry from A5, GeoHash, H3, Quadkey, S2, and full Google Plus Code identifiers. It also detects their conventional data-column names so visualization layers such as deck.gl-community's GlobalGridLayer can select the appropriate decoder.

- [@math.gl/dggs](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs.md): @math.gl/dggs provides a deliberately small JavaScript API for decoding cell geometry from A5, GeoHash, H3, Quadkey, S2, and full Google Plus Code identifiers. It also detects their conventional data-column names so visualization layers such as deck.gl-community's GlobalGridLayer can select the appropriate decoder.
- [@math.gl/dggs/a5](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs/api-reference/a5.md): A5Decoder is the lightweight A5 geometry adapter exported by @math.gl/dggs/a5. It accepts hexadecimal tokens and bigint indexes, and implements the common DGGSDecoder center, boundary, bounds, and token/index conversion methods.
- [@math.gl/dggs/decoders](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs/api-reference/decoders.md): DGGSDecoder defines the common API implemented by the decoder objects exported from @math.gl/dggs.
- [@math.gl/dggs/geohash](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs/api-reference/geohash.md): The GeoHash functions in math.gl are currently focused on decoding Geohash encoded data, not encoding it.
- [@math.gl/dggs/h3](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs/api-reference/h3.md): H3Decoder is the lightweight H3 geometry adapter exported by @math.gl/dggs/h3. It accepts hexadecimal H3 strings and bigint indexes, and implements the common DGGSDecoder center, boundary, bounds, and token/index conversion methods.
- [@math.gl/dggs/plus-code](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs/api-reference/plus-code.md): PlusCodeDecoder is a lightweight DGGS-like geometry adapter for Google Plus Codes, exported by @math.gl/dggs. It decodes a full Open Location Code into its center, rectangular boundary, and bounds.
- [@math.gl/dggs/quadkey](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs/api-reference/quadkey.md): QuadkeyDecoder is focused on decoding quadkeys.
- [@math.gl/dggs/s2](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs/api-reference/s2.md): Overview
- [Discrete Global Grids](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/dggs/developer-guide/dggs.md): Global grid encodings identify cells rather than individual coordinates. Use @math.gl/dggs to turn cell identifiers into longitude/latitude centers and boundaries for visualization.

#### earth

Earth models, sunlight, astronomy, time zones, and ocean calculations. Import each API from its feature subpath.

- [@math.gl/earth](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth.md): Earth models, sunlight, astronomy, time zones, and ocean calculations. Import each API from its feature subpath.
- [@math.gl/earth/geoid](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/geoid.md): The @math.gl/earth module evaluates geoid heights from Earth gravity model grids.
- [createGeoidFromGrid](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/geoid/api-reference/create-geoid-from-grid.md): Creates a Geoid from a complete global grid of decoded unsigned 16-bit samples.
- [Geoid](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/geoid/api-reference/geoid.md): class Geoid - "Gravity Height Model"
- [parsePGM](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/geoid/api-reference/parse-pgm.md): Parse a GeographicLib geoid PGM file into a Geoid. The parser requires one complete
- [Earth Models and Geoid Heights](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/geoid/developer-guide/geospatial-models.md): Use a sphere or ellipsoid for coordinate geometry, and a geoid model when converting between ellipsoidal and orthometric heights.
- [@math.gl/earth/ocean](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/ocean.md): @math.gl/earth/ocean supplies seawater and underwater-acoustics equations for browser
- [Seawater state](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/ocean/api-reference/seawater.md): A subset of TEOS-10, the international thermodynamic equation of seawater. Each function
- [Sound speed and absorption](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/ocean/api-reference/sound.md): Classic equations that survey software uses. Use them to reproduce existing results. For

- [Cloud lighting](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/earth/sun/api-reference/cloud-lighting.md): {/ SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT /}

Use it for map labels, daily aggregation, and scheduling. It uses the runtime's timezone rules; use Intl.DateTimeFormat for localized presentation.

#### geometry

The @math.gl/geometry module provides renderer-independent CPU mesh data and primitive

- [@math.gl/geometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry.md): The @math.gl/geometry module provides renderer-independent CPU mesh data and primitive
- [BoxGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/box-geometry.md): A box centered at the origin. size specifies positive total X, Y and Z lengths (default [1, 1, 1]).
- [CapsuleGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/capsule-geometry.md): The convex hull of endpoint spheres on the Y axis. height is the positive distance between sphere centers (default 1). radiusBottom and radiusTop default to 0.5; at least one must be positive. nradial, ncap and nvertical control tessellation (defaults 10, 5 and 1).
- [ConeGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/cone-geometry.md): A cone with a zero-radius top and its point at +Y by default. radius defaults to 0.5, height to 1, topCap to false and bottomCap to true. nradial and nvertical default to 10 and 1. verticalAxis may be x, y or z (default y).
- [CubeGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/cube-geometry.md): An equal-sided box centered at the origin. size is a positive total side length (default 1).
- [CylinderGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/cylinder-geometry.md): A closed Y-aligned cylinder, including tapered cylinders. height defaults to 2; radiusTop and radiusBottom default to 0.5. At least one radius must be positive. nradial and nvertical default to 10 and 1.
- [HingeTree 🧪](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/hinge-tree.md): Evaluates rigid panels connected by hinges, independently of mesh generation and rendering.
- [IcoSphereGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/ico-sphere-geometry.md): A sphere built by subdividing an icosahedron. Positive radius defaults to 0.5, and non-negative integer iterations defaults to 0. Each iteration subdivides each triangle into four.
- [Parametric geometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/parametric.md): This optional subpath returns ordinary Geometry instances with Float32 POSITION,
- [PlaneGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/plane-geometry.md): A finite plane in XZ, with its front face and normal pointing +Y. Positive finite sizeX and sizeZ are required. nx and nz control subdivisions, both defaulting to 1.
- [@math.gl/geometry/primitives](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/primitives.md): A renderer-independent CPU mesh container. The viewer accepts a Geometry instance through
- [PrismGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/prism-geometry.md): A closed regular polygon prism centered at the origin, with height along Y. Each
- [RingGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/ring-geometry.md): A solid annulus centered at the origin, with height along Y. Partial sweeps form
- [SphereGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/sphere-geometry.md): A latitude/longitude sphere centered at the origin. Positive radius defaults to 0.5. nlat and nlong default to 10 and control latitude and longitude segments.
- [TruncatedConeGeometry](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/api-reference/truncated-cone-geometry.md): A general tapered primitive with independent radii, caps and axis. topRadius and bottomRadius default to zero: supply at least one positive radius. height defaults to 1, both cap flags to false, nradial to 10, nvertical to 1, and verticalAxis to y.
- [@math.gl/geometry/culling](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling.md): @math.gl/geometry/culling tests bounding volumes against planes and provides analytic shape queries. Use it to reject objects outside a view frustum, intersect rays with shapes, and compute enclosing bounds.
- [AxisAlignedBoundingBox](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/axis-aligned-bounding-box.md): An AxisAlignedBoundingBox is a closed and convex cuboid that is aligned with the orthogonal axes.
- [BoundingSphere](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/bounding-sphere.md): A bounding sphere with a center and a radius.
- [BoundingVolume (Interface)](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/bounding-volume.md): An interface defining common operations for bounding volumes (i.e. BoundingSphere, AxisAlignedBoundingBox, OrientedBoundingBox).
- [BoxShape](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/box-shape.md): A box centered at the origin, with faces aligned to the local axes.
- [CapsuleShape](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/capsule-shape.md): The convex hull of two spheres centered at [0, -height / 2, 0] and [0, height / 2, 0].
- [CullingVolume](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/culling-volume.md): A culling volume defined by planes.
- [CylinderShape](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/cylinder-shape.md): A capped cylinder centered at the origin along the local Y axis.
- [Bounds, frusta and geometric queries](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/extended-queries.md): These functions are exported from both @math.gl/geometry and
- [intersectOrientedBoxes2D](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/intersect-oriented-boxes-2d.md): Test two oriented rectangles in a shared two-dimensional Euclidean coordinate space. This
- [OrientedBoundingBox](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/oriented-bounding-box.md): An OrientedBoundingBox is a closed and convex cuboid. It can provide a tighter bounding volume than a bounding sphere or an axis aligned bounding box in many cases.
- [Plane](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/plane.md): A plane in Hessian Normal Form defined by ax + by + cz + d = 0 where [a, b, c] is the plane's normal, d is the signed distance to the plane (from the origin along the normal), and [x, y, z] is any point on the plane.
- [PlaneShape](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/plane-shape.md): A surface in the local XZ plane facing +Y. The negative-Y half-space is inside.
- [Ray and closest-point queries](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/queries.md): Import unprojectScreenRay, intersectRayBounds, intersectRayTriangle, and getClosestPointOnTriangle from
- [Ray](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/ray.md): A ray that extends infinitely from an origin in one direction.
- [Shape](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/shapes.md): Shape is the shared interface for analytic containment, ray intersection, and bounding-volume queries. Import it as a type from @math.gl/geometry or @math.gl/geometry/culling. The existing name ImplicitShape remains available.
- [SphereShape](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/culling/api-reference/sphere-shape.md): A sphere centered at the local origin.
- [@math.gl/geometry/curves](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/curves.md): The curves module provides renderer-independent parametric curves for 2D and 3D Cartesian
- [CurveArcLength](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/curves/api-reference/curve-arc-length.md): Constructor
- [Curve classes](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/curves/api-reference/curves.md): Constructors

- [@math.gl/geometry/arrow](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geometry/entry-points/arrow.md): Tessellate GeoArrow polygons into triangle meshes. Use tessellateGeoArrowPolygons for a column or tessellateGeoArrowStream for a stream. Create GeoArrow columns with @math.gl/core/arrow.

#### geospatial

@math.gl/geospatial provides ellipsoid geometry, geographic/Cartesian conversions, local tangent frames, globe queries, and tile-grid geometry. Use it for WGS84 positions and 3D Tiles bounds without a renderer dependency.

- [@math.gl/geospatial](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geospatial.md): @math.gl/geospatial provides ellipsoid geometry, geographic/Cartesian conversions, local tangent frames, globe queries, and tile-grid geometry. Use it for WGS84 positions and 3D Tiles bounds without a renderer dependency.

- [Review of all 49 retained PROJ findings](https://visgl.github.io/math.gl/next/docs/modules/geospatial/projection/pole-findings-review.md): Every configuration with a finding at revision 64b7fe33 is listed below. The review found real accuracy gaps in seven kernels: LAEA, stereographic, oblique stereographic, spherical AEQD, QSC, Mollweide and polyconic. 22 of the 49 configurations receive a numerical fix. Some have both a fixed math.gl error and a separate retained oracle/domain difference.

It provides scales, convergence, distortion and coordinate derivatives without importing projection algorithms. Supply the same projection plugin and geometry used by your map.
